questions.q: What does React Native create when you render <View><Text>Hello</Text></View>?
options: Real native views (a UIView on iOS, a ViewGroup on Android) kept in sync with the component tree
An HTML div inside a hidden web view
A canvas the JS engine draws pixels onto
A compiled copy of your code in Swift and Kotlin
questions.explain: React Native keeps a tree of real platform views in sync with your React tree; nothing is drawn in a browser.

questions.q: Which thread keeps a native ScrollView scrolling even while your JavaScript is busy for 200 ms?
options: The UI (main) thread, because scrolling is handled natively
questions.explain: Scrolling lives on the UI thread, so it does not need JavaScript. Taps that need new JS state do wait for the JS thread.

questions.q: What is Expo Go?
options: A pre-built app that loads your JavaScript without you compiling native code, limited to the native modules Expo ships
A cloud service that compiles your app for the stores
questions.explain: Expo Go is great for starting out, but it only contains Expo's own native modules. Development builds remove that limit.

questions.q: What is Hermes?
options: The JavaScript engine used by default in React Native, which compiles your JS to bytecode at build time
questions.explain: Hermes was built by Meta for React Native; precompiled bytecode means less parsing at launch.

questions.q: What happens if you write <View>Hello</View>?
options: It renders Hello only on Android
It fails with 'Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component'
It renders Hello in the default font
It renders nothing and logs a warning
questions.explain: In React Native every string must live inside a <Text>.

questions.q: Given const unread = 0, what is wrong with <View>{unread && <Text>new</Text>}</View>?
options: The expression evaluates to the number 0, which is rendered as a bare string and crashes on native
It only fails in release builds
questions.explain: Make the condition a real boolean, for example unread > 0 &&.

questions.q: Why must a remote <Image source={{ uri }} /> be given a width and height?
options: React Native cannot know the size of a remote image at build time, so without a size it has zero size
It is only a style recommendation
questions.explain: Bundled assets via require() have dimensions known to Metro; remote images do not.

questions.q: Which props make nested <Text> inside <Text> inherit the parent's font size and colour?
options: None needed: nested Text inherits style from its parent, the only place React Native styles inherit
questions.explain: React Native has no CSS cascade except for nested Text.

questions.q: What unit do numeric style values like fontSize: 16 use?
options: Density-independent pixels (dp on Android, points on iOS)
questions.explain: The same number gives the same physical size on low- and high-density screens.

questions.q: Which style prop correctly adds a border?
options: borderWidth together with borderColor (and optionally borderStyle)
questions.explain: The CSS border shorthand does not exist in React Native.

questions.q: What does style={[styles.card, selected && styles.cardSelected]} do?
options: Applies both styles at the same time regardless of selected
Applies the card style, and also the selected style when selected is truthy (later entries win, falsy entries are ignored)
questions.explain: Style arrays replace CSS modifier classes.

questions.q: How do you implement dark mode styling in React Native?
options: It is automatic for every View
In JavaScript, for example with useColorScheme and a theme object, since there are no media queries
questions.explain: There are no pseudo-classes or media queries; they are done with state and hooks.

questions.q: What is the default flexDirection in React Native?
questions.explain: Phones are tall, so the default differs from the web's row.

questions.q: Your root View has no flex: 1 and its background only covers half the screen. Why?
options: Without flex: 1 it is only as tall as its content
The screen has a safe area
backgroundColor is not supported on root views
questions.explain: flex: 1 makes a view fill the available space.

questions.q: Siblings with flex: 2 and flex: 1 share the remaining space in what ratio?
questions.explain: flex with a positive number n behaves like flexGrow n, flexShrink 1 and flexBasis 0.

questions.q: Which property positions children along the cross axis?
questions.explain: justifyContent works on the main axis; alignItems on the cross axis.

questions.q: Why is Pressable preferred over TouchableOpacity in new code?
options: TouchableOpacity was removed from the language
It is the single modern component, with pressed state functions, Android ripple and hitSlop, replacing the older Touchable family
Pressable runs natively and the others run in JS
questions.explain: Pressable replaces the older components you still see in old code.

questions.q: For a long press, what happens after delayLongPress elapses?
options: onLongPress fires and onPress does not
questions.explain: Press-and-hold triggers onLongPress instead of onPress.

questions.q: A 20-point icon is hard to tap. What is the idiomatic fix that does not change layout?
options: Add hitSlop to extend the touch area invisibly
questions.explain: Platform guidance suggests at least about 44x44 points (Apple) or 48x48 dp (Android).

questions.q: What does android_ripple do on iOS?
questions.explain: Combine it with a pressed style for iOS.

questions.q: Which keyboard type shows a numeric pad without a decimal point?
questions.explain: decimal-pad adds the decimal separator.

questions.q: Why should an email field set autoCapitalize="none"?
options: iOS would otherwise capitalise the first letter and login can fail
questions.explain: Also turn off autoCorrect for emails and usernames.

questions.q: How do you move focus to the next field when the user presses the return key?
options: Use refs and call nextRef.current?.focus() in onSubmitEditing, with returnKeyType="next"
The OS does it automatically for every TextInput
questions.explain: You handle submit behaviour with refs.

questions.q: What does onChangeText give you?
options: The new text as a string directly
questions.explain: onChange gives a native event whose nativeEvent.text holds the same thing.

questions.q: Why use FlatList instead of mapping 2,000 items inside a ScrollView?
options: FlatList is the only component that can show text
FlatList virtualizes, rendering only items near the screen and saving memory
It makes the data load faster from the network
questions.explain: Mounting thousands of native views is slow and can get the app killed.

questions.q: When is it wrong to use the item's index as keyExtractor?
options: When items can be inserted, removed or reordered, because React will reuse the wrong row's state
questions.explain: Use a stable unique ID.

questions.q: Why should a vertical FlatList not be nested inside a vertical ScrollView?
options: The outer ScrollView gives it unlimited height so it renders everything and virtualization is lost
FlatList cannot render in a ScrollView at all
It disables pull to refresh only
questions.explain: Use ListHeaderComponent and ListFooterComponent for extra content.

questions.q: Which prop shows a message when the list has no items?
questions.explain: It renders when data is empty.

questions.q: What is the safe area?
options: The part of the screen not covered by system UI such as the notch, status bar and home indicator
The memory region for the JS engine
The area where touches always register
questions.explain: Use react-native-safe-area-context to respect it.

questions.q: Which hook reads safe-area insets in react-native-safe-area-context?
questions.explain: It is handy for headers and footers that paint under system UI.

questions.q: Which is the right way to branch on platform for a small value?
questions.explain: For larger differences use .ios.tsx and .android.tsx files.

questions.q: Which hook gives the current screen size and updates on rotation?
questions.explain: The hook re-renders when dimensions change.

questions.q: How do you open React Native DevTools from the terminal running Expo?
questions.explain: It connects Chrome DevTools to the Hermes engine.

questions.q: In a LogBox error overlay, how should you read the component stack?
options: Bottom-up: the bottom component rendered the one above it, so the cause is near the top entry
questions.explain: The component stack often tells you more than the JS stack.

questions.q: What happened to the old 'Remote JS Debugging' mode?
options: It is available only on Android
It is gone from current React Native; DevTools attaches to Hermes on the device instead
questions.explain: Running JS in Chrome changed timing and hid real bugs.

questions.q: A bug appears only in a release build. What is the correct first move?
options: Reproduce it in a release build and read native logs and crash reports, since release differs from development
questions.explain: Release builds minify, optimise and skip development checks.
Three consecutive days ending today. Verified by running it in Node.
The streak counts from yesterday if today is not done yet, so it is not broken until the day ends. Verified by running it in Node.
addDays goes through new Date(y, m-1, d+delta), so month boundaries are handled. Verified by running it in Node.

questions.q: Why does the project store dates as local YYYY-MM-DD strings instead of Date objects?
options: Strings are faster to sort in SQL only
Date does not exist in Hermes
It avoids time-zone surprises from comparing Date objects created at different times of day
questions.explain: A day key is the same however and whenever it is created.

questions.q: What happens to the List screen when you push Details onto a stack?
options: List stays mounted underneath, keeping its state and scroll position
It unmounts and re-fetches when you come back
It is paused and cannot hold state
questions.explain: Screens under the top of a stack stay mounted.

questions.q: What is the usual structure for a tab navigator?
options: One shared stack for all tabs
Each tab holds its own stack so each keeps an independent history
Tabs always unmount when you leave them
questions.explain: Switching tabs keeps each tab's place.

questions.q: What is a modal screen for?
options: A self-contained task presented over everything else, such as composing or adding an item, which is dismissed rather than navigated back from
questions.explain: Modals rise from the bottom and are dismissed downward.

questions.q: Why does a stack keeping screens mounted matter for state design?
options: A state change can re-render screens the user cannot see, so subscribe narrowly
It forces you to use Redux
questions.explain: This idea returns in the app-state lesson.

questions.q: In Expo Router, what does a file app/settings/notifications.tsx define?
questions.explain: Every file in app/ is a route.

questions.q: What does _layout.tsx define?
options: The navigator (for example Stack or Tabs) for its folder
questions.explain: Layouts default-export a navigator.

questions.q: Which element shows unmatched URLs?
questions.explain: It is a special file in app/.

questions.q: What is the difference between router.push and router.replace?
options: push adds a screen to the stack; replace swaps the current screen without growing history
questions.explain: Use replace for flows like sign-in where back should not return.

questions.q: What does the file app/habit/[id].tsx mean?
options: A dynamic route where id is a parameter, such as /habit/42
questions.explain: Read it with useLocalSearchParams.

questions.q: If you navigate with params: { count: 3 }, what type is count on the receiving screen?
options: It depends on the TypeScript generic
string, because URL params are strings
questions.explain: The generic is a promise to TypeScript, not a runtime check; parse and validate.

questions.q: What belongs in route params?
options: A whole habit object serialised to JSON
Identifiers and view state such as an id, tab, filter or sort
questions.explain: Objects in URLs bloat them and go stale.

questions.q: Why prefer useLocalSearchParams over useGlobalSearchParams?
options: Local params are typed and global are not
Global params re-render background screens whenever the user navigates anywhere
questions.explain: Screens stay mounted, so global params cause extra renders.
Toggling twice removes d1; d2 is then added. Verified by running it in Node.

questions.q: Where should a search box's text live?
options: In local useState in the component, not in a global store
questions.explain: Putting keystrokes in global state re-renders the whole app.

questions.q: Why do Zustand selectors help in React Native apps?
options: A component re-renders only when the selected slice changes, which matters because screens stay mounted
They run on the UI thread
questions.explain: Subscribe to exactly what each screen needs.

questions.q: Which kind of state belongs in a data-fetching cache such as TanStack Query?
options: Server state owned by a backend
questions.explain: Do not copy server data into a global store where it goes stale.

questions.q: What does the queryKey identify?
options: The cached data; components using the same key share one cache entry and request
questions.explain: Include every input of the query in the key, such as the search term.

questions.q: Why must a queryFn throw on a non-OK response?
options: fetch does not reject on HTTP errors like 500, so you must throw for Query to see an error
questions.explain: Check res.ok and throw.

questions.q: What does the API quirk 'meals: null' for no results mean for your client?
options: Normalise it to an empty array in your API layer
questions.explain: Keep API oddities out of components.

questions.q: What does staleTime control?
options: How long a request can run
How long data stays in memory before deletion
How long fetched data is considered fresh before a background refetch is allowed
questions.explain: Cached data renders instantly while stale data refetches in the background.

questions.q: Where should an auth token be stored?
options: A JSON file in the documents folder
questions.explain: AsyncStorage is unencrypted; treat it like a text file.

questions.q: Which store suits records you filter, sort and join?
questions.explain: AsyncStorage is for small key-value data.

questions.q: Why does the prefs example merge saved JSON with defaultPrefs?
options: Adding a new preference in a later version does not break users who saved the old shape
questions.explain: Defensive loading with try/catch also protects against corrupt JSON.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a version in a key like 'prefs:v1' or in SQLite user_version?
options: It lets a breaking change migrate data from one schema to the next
questions.explain: Versioned migrations keep existing users' data safe.

questions.q: What does z.coerce.number() do in a form schema?
options: Turns the string from a TextInput into a number, then validates it
questions.explain: TextInput values are always strings.

questions.q: What is .refine used for?
options: Cross-field or custom rules, with a path so the error attaches to the right field
questions.explain: For example: end date must be after start date.

questions.q: Why does comparing 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings with >= work?
options: It works only for leap years
The format sorts lexicographically in date order
JavaScript has date strings built in
questions.explain: A neat benefit of ISO-style dates.

questions.q: What do z.input and z.output give you?
options: Two types: the raw form values and the parsed result
questions.explain: For example string vs number after coercion.

questions.q: What does an @2x and @3x file next to image.png do?
options: They make the app larger on all devices
Metro picks the variant matching the device density automatically
questions.explain: Layout uses the 1x size in points.

questions.q: Why can't you write require(`./icons/${name}.png`)?
options: require paths must be static strings that Metro resolves at bundle time; use a map of requires
questions.explain: Build an object of static requires.

questions.q: What does cachePolicy="memory-disk" give you in expo-image?
options: Decoded images in memory and files on disk so scrolling back or reopening does not refetch
questions.explain: Plus placeholders like BlurHash and transitions.

questions.q: What is a BlurHash?
options: A short string that decodes to a blurry preview shown while the real image loads
questions.explain: Generate it on the server when the image is uploaded.

questions.q: On iOS, what does the software keyboard do to your layout?
options: Nothing: the keyboard covers it and you must move content yourself
questions.explain: Use KeyboardAvoidingView or insets.

questions.q: Which KeyboardAvoidingView behavior is the most predictable on iOS?
questions.explain: It adds bottom padding equal to the keyboard height.

questions.q: What is keyboardVerticalOffset for?
options: Compensating for anything above the view, usually the navigation header
questions.explain: Wrong values leave the composer hidden or floating.

questions.q: Why is edge-to-edge relevant to keyboard handling on Android?
options: The app draws behind system bars and the keyboard is reported as an inset, so you often must handle it explicitly
questions.explain: Test on both platforms, ideally on a real device.

questions.q: Why are favourites stored with the full recipe JSON in SQLite?
options: So a favourited recipe opens offline
questions.explain: Network first, local fallback.

questions.q: What does the recipe detail deep link recipebook://recipe/52785 require?
options: A URL scheme configured in app.json and a route app/recipe/[id].tsx
questions.explain: Expo Router gives every screen a URL.

questions.q: What is an optimistic update for the favourite heart?
options: Update the UI immediately and roll back if the write fails
questions.explain: It feels instant.

questions.q: Why is loadRecipe written as a pure function?
options: It can be tested without React or a device
Pure functions are faster in Hermes
questions.explain: Pure logic is the cheapest layer to test.

questions.q: Roughly how long is the per-frame budget at 60 Hz?
questions.explain: Higher refresh rates leave less.

questions.q: How did the old bridge communicate between JS and native?
options: By serialising calls to JSON and flushing them asynchronously in a queue
questions.explain: This caused overhead and prevented synchronous calls.

questions.q: What does JSI let JavaScript do in the New Architecture?
options: Hold direct references to native objects and call them, including synchronously, without JSON serialisation
questions.explain: JSI underpins Fabric and TurboModules.

questions.q: Since which React Native version is the New Architecture the default?
questions.explain: Older libraries may still need compatibility work.

questions.q: Which can you NOT test properly on the iOS Simulator?
options: Camera and haptics (use a real device)
questions.explain: Simulators are not phones.

questions.q: What is a good use of haptics?
options: Tie them to meaningful state changes such as a habit completed, using the semantic types
questions.explain: Users can disable system haptics, in which case calls do nothing.

questions.q: What does getLastKnownPositionAsync give you?
options: A cheap, instant but possibly old position, good for a first guess
questions.explain: getCurrentPositionAsync with accuracy Balanced gets a fresh fix.

questions.q: What battery trade-off applies to location?
options: Higher accuracy and continuous updates use more battery, so pick the lowest accuracy that works
questions.explain: Choose accuracy for the feature.

questions.q: On iOS, how many times is a permission's system prompt shown?
options: At most once; later requests return denied immediately
questions.explain: After that only Settings can change it.

questions.q: What does canAskAgain: false mean?
options: The system will not show a prompt again, so send the user to Settings
questions.explain: Explain why and link to Settings.

questions.q: When should you ask for notification permission?
options: When the user turns on a reminder, with context, not at first launch
questions.explain: Ask at the moment of value.

questions.q: What happens on iOS if an app requests a permission without a usage description string?
options: It crashes (and App Review rejects vague strings)
questions.explain: Set strings in config plugins.

questions.q: What is a local notification?
options: One scheduled on the device by your app, with no server needed
questions.explain: Remote push comes from a server.

questions.q: What do Android notification channels do?
options: Group notifications so users can control them separately in system settings
questions.explain: Create a channel before requesting permission on Android 13+.

questions.q: By default, what happens to a notification that arrives while your app is open?
options: It is not shown unless you set a notification handler
questions.explain: Use setNotificationHandler once at startup.

questions.q: Where can remote push be tested?
options: On a physical device, using a development build rather than Expo Go on Android
questions.explain: iOS also needs an Apple Developer account for APNs credentials.

questions.q: Which properties can the Animated native driver animate?
options: Non-layout properties such as transform and opacity
questions.explain: Layout properties need the JS driver.

questions.q: What are Reanimated worklets?
options: Small JavaScript functions run on the UI thread in a separate JS runtime
questions.explain: useAnimatedStyle's callback is one.

questions.q: What is a shared value?
options: State both threads can read and write, used to drive animations
questions.explain: Created with useSharedValue.

questions.q: Which function describes a spring-style move of a shared value?
questions.explain: Others include withTiming, withDecay, withSequence.

questions.q: Why does Gesture Handler feel smoother than the built-in responder system?
options: It recognises gestures natively on the UI thread, so a busy JS thread does not make gestures sticky
questions.explain: Paired with Reanimated, the loop avoids JS.

questions.q: What must wrap your app to use Gesture Handler?
options: GestureHandlerRootView as close to the root as possible
questions.explain: With flex: 1.

questions.q: How do you attach a gesture to a view?
options: Build it with Gesture.Pan() etc. and pass it to GestureDetector
questions.explain: The 2.x builder API.

questions.q: Why should you let npx expo install choose the Gesture Handler version?
options: It picks the version matching your SDK, which may differ from npm's latest major
questions.explain: APIs differ between majors.

questions.q: What does a screen reader announce for a focused element, roughly in order?
options: Label, role, state, then optional hint
questions.explain: Give each interactive element all four.

questions.q: Which prop sets the spoken name of an icon-only button?
questions.explain: It defaults to text content.

questions.q: Which prop describes checked or disabled?
questions.explain: Keep it in sync with the visual state.

questions.q: What should you do for users who enable Reduce Motion?
options: Reduce or skip non-essential animation, for example by checking the setting
questions.explain: Respect the OS accessibility settings.

questions.q: When should you write a native module?
options: When you need a platform capability that no maintained library provides
To make JS faster without profiling
questions.explain: Check Expo SDK and React Native Directory first.

questions.q: What does the Expo Modules API let you write?
options: Native modules in Swift and Kotlin with a declarative DSL
questions.explain: It generates the JSI bindings for you.

questions.q: What does create-expo-module --local do?
options: Scaffolds a module inside your app's modules/ folder, autolinked
questions.explain: Local modules live in your repo.

questions.q: Why does a native module require a rebuild?
options: Native code changes are compiled into the binary and cannot be hot-reloaded or sent over the air
questions.explain: Use a development build.

questions.q: What is a development build?
options: Your own debug app containing exactly your native dependencies, with the same dev tools as Expo Go
questions.explain: Use expo-dev-client.

questions.q: What does npx expo prebuild do?
options: Generates the ios/ and android/ projects from a template, app config and config plugins
questions.explain: Continuous Native Generation lets you not commit them.

questions.q: When do you rebuild the development build?
options: When the native side changes: dependencies or config
questions.explain: JS changes use Fast Refresh.

questions.q: What is a config plugin?
options: Code that edits native project files such as Info.plist or the manifest during prebuild
questions.explain: Library authors and you can write them.

questions.q: In Field Notes, why is every note saved locally first?
options: Saving must never depend on the network; syncing happens afterwards
questions.explain: Offline-first design.

questions.q: Why are photos copied out of the cache into the document directory?
options: The OS can delete cache files; documents persist
questions.explain: Persist what matters.

questions.q: What is exponential backoff in sync retries?
options: Waiting progressively longer after each failure before retrying
questions.explain: It avoids hammering a struggling server.

questions.q: How do you avoid uploading the same note version twice?
options: Track sync state and version per note and make the upload idempotent
questions.explain: Never upload twice for the same version.

questions.q: Where should you measure performance?
options: Development build on the newest iPhone
In a release build on a low-to-mid-range Android phone
questions.explain: Development builds are much slower.

questions.q: JS frame rate drops but UI frame rate is fine. What does that suggest?
options: JavaScript is doing too much, such as heavy renders or big parsing
questions.explain: Taps feel delayed; scrolling stays smooth.

questions.q: Which tool shows why a component re-rendered?
options: React DevTools Profiler with 'Record why each component rendered'
questions.explain: Open DevTools with j.

questions.q: A whole list re-renders when one item changes. Typical fix?
options: memo the row, use stable callbacks and keep item identity stable
questions.explain: Measure again after the change.

questions.q: What does getItemLayout enable?
options: Skips measurement and makes scrollToIndex exact, for fixed or computable row heights
questions.explain: It tells the list size and offset up front.

questions.q: What does windowSize control?
options: How many screen-heights of content stay mounted (default 21)
questions.explain: Lower saves memory but may show blanks on fast flings.

questions.q: How does FlashList differ from FlatList?
options: It recycles views instead of mounting and unmounting them
questions.explain: Set recyclingKey and use item types.

questions.q: What is the first step before tuning list props?
options: Fix the rows: memoise, keep them shallow, size images and avoid heavy render work
questions.explain: No setting rescues a slow row.

questions.q: In RNTL 14, how do you call render?
options: await render(...), because render is async
questions.explain: Forgetting await gives 'render function has not been called'.

questions.q: What does the jest-expo preset do?
options: Configures Babel like Metro, sets up React Native mocks and mocks native Expo modules
questions.explain: Tests run in Node.

questions.q: In which order should you prefer queries?
options: By role, label and text as users find them, before testID
questions.explain: Query like a user.

questions.q: What do component tests NOT tell you?
options: Whether a function returns the right value
Whether the compiled app launches, native modules link or the keyboard covers a button
questions.explain: That needs E2E.

questions.q: How does Maestro drive the app?
options: From outside through the accessibility layer, with YAML flows
questions.explain: Black box.

questions.q: How does Detox synchronise with the app?
options: It tracks the app's busy state and waits until idle
questions.explain: Grey box.

questions.q: Why write few E2E tests?
options: They are slower and more fragile, so cover journeys that must never break
questions.explain: Sign-in, core create flow, purchase.

questions.q: What is testID for?
options: A stable handle for elements without stable text, mapped to the accessibility identifier or resource-id
questions.explain: Prefer labels and visible text first.

questions.q: What happens to a value set as EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPS_KEY?
options: It is only in Expo Go
It is inlined into the JS bundle and visible to anyone who unpacks the app
It stays on the build server
questions.explain: The lesson found it as plain text in the Hermes bytecode.

questions.q: Where must private keys such as payment secrets live?
options: On your server, which the app calls after authenticating the user
questions.explain: Hiding a button does not protect an endpoint.

questions.q: Where does mobile security ultimately live?
options: On the server, because the attacker controls the device
questions.explain: The app protects user data on the device.

questions.q: What should you do with deep-link parameters?
questions.explain: Treat links like any external input.

questions.q: What does an iOS .ipa vs Android .aab refer to?
options: The signed release binaries for the App Store and Google Play
questions.explain: Play uses Android App Bundles.

questions.q: What is the eas.json preview profile typically used for?
options: Internal release-mode builds for QA and performance testing
questions.explain: An APK on Android.

questions.q: What does appVersionSource: remote mean?
questions.explain: With autoIncrement for production.

questions.q: Why keep your keystore and credentials safe?
options: Losing signing credentials can block updates to an existing app (Play App Signing reduces the risk)
questions.explain: Let EAS manage credentials.

questions.q: What does TestFlight give you?
options: A beta stage where internal testers install immediately and external testers need a lightweight review
questions.explain: The closest thing to production.

questions.q: What must apps with account creation also provide?
options: A way to delete the account in the app
questions.explain: Apple and Google both require a path.

questions.q: What do you give reviewers if your app needs login?
options: A demo account in the review notes
questions.explain: Reviewers must reach all features.

questions.q: Why use staged rollouts?
options: So a bad release reaches only a fraction of users first
questions.explain: Watch crashes and ramp up.

questions.q: What can an OTA update change?
options: The JavaScript bundle and its assets
questions.explain: Native changes need a new binary.

questions.q: What is runtime version for?
options: A build only accepts updates with the same runtime version, protecting against JS/native mismatch
questions.explain: Mismatch would crash.

questions.q: What does the fingerprint policy do?
options: Hashes everything affecting the native build so the runtime version changes only when native code changes
questions.explain: A JS-only change does not change it.

questions.q: What are OTA updates NOT meant for?
options: Changing the app's primary purpose or swapping in a different app after review
questions.explain: Stay within store rules.

questions.q: What do route ErrorBoundaries catch?
options: Errors thrown while rendering a route's subtree
questions.explain: Handle the others in place and with a reporter.

questions.q: Why upload source maps to Sentry?
options: So production stack traces map back to your readable source
questions.explain: Tag releases to match builds.

questions.q: What is a sensible analytics approach?
options: Collect a small amount, respectfully and with consent where required
questions.explain: Declare it in privacy labels.

questions.q: What does __DEV__ allow in the error screen?
options: Show details in development and a friendly message in release
questions.explain: Do not leak internals to users.

questions.q: What is the capstone's deliverable?
options: Evidence that the app is a release candidate: tests, accessibility, performance, release setup and monitoring
questions.explain: It is about readiness.

questions.q: What goes in ARCHITECTURE.md?
options: Where state lives, data flows, offline behaviour and the navigation tree
questions.explain: One page a reviewer can follow.

questions.q: What should E2E flows cover in the capstone?
options: Add habit, complete it, relaunch and still completed; and the permission-denied reminder path
questions.explain: Few, valuable flows.

questions.q: What does a preflight script help with?
options: Checking the release gates automatically before you submit
questions.explain: Catch mistakes early.

questions.q: A React Native app feels native mainly because...
options: its component tree is mapped to real platform views, and scrolling, text and accessibility come from the OS
it runs Swift and Kotlin translations of your JS at runtime
it is compiled to a web page that looks like an app
it draws everything itself on a canvas
questions.explain: Components map to native views; that is also why div, CSS files and onClick do not exist.

questions.q: A tap handler updates state but the UI responds 300 ms late, while scrolling stays smooth. Which is the likely cause?
options: The UI thread is overloaded by shadows
The JS thread is busy (heavy render or computation); scrolling runs on the UI thread
questions.explain: JS frame rate dropping with UI fine points to JavaScript work.

questions.q: Which pair is the correct fix for 'my background only covers half the screen' and 'my list doesn't scroll'?
options: Give the root View and the list's parent flex: 1 so they receive a bounded height
questions.explain: Without flex: 1 a view is only as tall as its content.

questions.q: What is the safest way to render a count badge only when unread > 0?
options: Return the number directly in a View
questions.explain: A 0 left of && is rendered as a bare string and crashes inside a View.

questions.q: Which approach gives native-feeling press feedback on both platforms?
options: Pressable with a pressed style (iOS) and android_ripple (Android), plus accessibilityRole and label
questions.explain: Pressable replaces the older Touchable family.

questions.q: A search screen stores the text in a global store and the whole app re-renders on every keystroke. What is the better design?
options: Keep the text in local useState and put only shared data in the store, with narrow selectors
questions.explain: Match each kind of state to the right place.

questions.q: Which store holds a refresh token?
questions.explain: AsyncStorage is unencrypted; treat it like a text file.

questions.q: Why does data fetched with TanStack Query appear instantly when you return to a screen?
options: It is cached by query key and renders from the cache while stale data refetches in the background
questions.explain: Server state is a cache you do not own.

questions.q: A form field holds the string '3' but your schema needs a number. What does the schema do?
questions.explain: TextInput values are always strings.

questions.q: What is the correct pattern for an offline-friendly detail screen?
options: Try the network, fall back to the locally stored copy and tell the user it is an offline copy
questions.explain: Store the full record when favouriting.

questions.q: Which statement about the New Architecture is true?
options: JSI lets JS call native objects directly without JSON serialisation, enabling synchronous calls
It adds a faster JSON bridge
questions.explain: Fabric and TurboModules build on JSI.

questions.q: An iOS user denied the camera permission last week. What can your app do?
options: Explain the benefit and send the user to Settings, because the system will not prompt again
questions.explain: canAskAgain false means Settings only.

questions.q: Which animation is safe to run with useNativeDriver: true?
options: A transform scale or an opacity fade
questions.explain: The native driver supports non-layout properties.

questions.q: A swipe-to-complete gesture must stay smooth while JS is busy. What do you use?
options: Gesture Handler plus Reanimated, so recognition and animation run on the UI thread
questions.explain: Callbacks are worklets.

questions.q: What is the right accessibility setup for an icon-only delete button?
options: accessibilityRole="button" with accessibilityLabel="Delete" and a large enough touch target
questions.explain: Label, role, state, then hint.

questions.q: A teammate adds a library with native code. How do you test it?
options: Create a development build; Expo Go only includes Expo's own native modules
questions.explain: Rebuild only when native dependencies or config change.

questions.q: A bug is only in the release build. What is your first step?
options: Reproduce it in a release build and check native crash logs and the Sentry report with source maps
questions.explain: Development and release differ a lot.

questions.q: Which JS-only fix can ship over the air, and which cannot?
options: A copy or logic fix can; a new native module or permission string cannot
questions.explain: Runtime version ties updates to compatible binaries.

questions.q: Which belongs in the app bundle?
options: Only keys that are safe to be public; real secrets stay on the server
questions.explain: EXPO_PUBLIC_ values are inlined into the bundle and readable.

challenges.title: Habit statistics: current streak, longest streak and weekly rate
challenges.prompt: Implement currentStreak, longestStreak and weeklyRate for habits whose check-ins are local YYYY-MM-DD strings. Handle duplicates, month boundaries and leap days. This is plain JavaScript logic — the kind you would put in a pure module and unit-test with Jest before wiring it into a React Native screen.
challenges.expected:
Read: current 2, longest 5, week 86%
Run: current 1, longest 1, week 14%
Stretch: current 0, longest 0, week 0%
Water: current 3, longest 3, week 43%
3
challenges.explain: Day keys are built with new Date(y, m-1, d+delta), which rolls over months and leap days correctly. longestStreak sorts unique keys and extends a run while the next day follows the previous one. Verified by running the solution in Node; React Native itself was not needed because this logic is deliberately independent of the UI.

challenges.title: Offline sync queue with exponential backoff
challenges.prompt: Implement backoff and SyncQueue so notes saved offline upload later with retries, never upload the same id:version twice, and a re-saved note becomes a new version. Time is passed in as a number so the behaviour is deterministic; there is no real network here.
challenges.expected:
t=0 a:1 failed (retry at 1000)
t=0 b:1 synced
t=1000 a:1 failed (retry at 3000)
t=3000 a:1 failed (retry at 7000)
t=7000 a:1 synced
t=8000 b:2 synced
calls 6 states av1:synced bv2:synced
1000,2000,4000,8000,8000,8000
challenges.explain: Each failure doubles the wait up to a cap, nextAt gates retries, and the sent set keyed by id:version makes uploads idempotent. This is a simulation with a fake uploader and fake clock, not a real device or network; verified by running it in Node.
